glm.feedback:
The diff faithfully implements the operator report: the field, its constant, the re-export, the submit wiring, and the request-body type field are all removed; the spec (FR-01.74) and `architecture.md` are updated to match; negative-existence assertions were added in both unit and E2E layers across both `codexIntegrationMode` values. The M1 wording fix (inherit note naming "sol", dropping the now-false "type any slug" clause) is present. I found no correctness, security, or regression issues — the deleted "Claude-runtime leak" test covered a path that no longer exists (nothing can write `codexImplementationModel` into `paramValues` anymore), so its removal loses no real coverage.

Findings:

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/external/NewIssueModal/payload-launch.codex-model.test.tsx (~line 34)
  Finding: The renamed first test ("never renders an Implementation-model field for a Codex-runtime launch") only renders the modal and asserts absence — it never submits, so despite living in a file about the POST body and replacing a body-threading test, it validates nothing about the launch payload. It's also redundant with the render-absence tests in the other three files. The behavior it nominally replaced (body wiring) is only covered in Codex Light mode by the second test; no test asserts the body for a Codextender-mode launch.
  Suggestion: Either delete this test (pure duplication) or make it a Codextender-mode variant of the second test that actually clicks launch and asserts `codexImplementationModel` is absent from the captured body.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/external/NewIssueModal/payload-launch.codex-model.test.tsx (deleted third test)
  Finding: The stale-`paramValues` leak test was deleted on the theory that nothing can set the key anymore. That is true for the current component, but `useNewIssueFormSubmit` still has the generic `paramValues` → body-threading machinery (`trimmedCodexParam` for the two surviving keys), so the guard is now only enforced by component structure, not by a test. A future field reusing the old key string would silently regress with no failing test.
  Suggestion: Optional: keep a single cheap assertion (in the "never sends" test) that a `paramValues` entry containing the literal key `"codex-implementation-model"` pre-seeded via the action's `parameters` still doesn't produce a `codexImplementationModel` body field — cheap insurance against the wiring creeping back.

Nothing else: server-side acceptance of `codexImplementationModel` is explicitly an accepted, disclosed gap per the spec; the compliance-artifact drift is disclosed as resolved by F5b regen.

Overall assessment: ship-as-is — the removal is complete and consistent across UI, wiring, types, spec, and docs; the two findings are optional test-hardening refinements, not defects.
